recent_posts.title: 60% of MD5 password hashes can be cracked in under an hour
recent_posts.summary: Research findings show that 60% of MD5 password hashes can be cracked in under an hour, highlighting the continued danger of using MD5 for password storage. Published on World Password Day, the report underscores the urgency of moving away from weak hashing algorithms and toward stronger authentication methods.

recent_posts.title: Survey finds 13% of employees willing to sell workplace login credentials
recent_posts.summary: A survey reveals that 1 in 8 employees (13%) consider selling their workplace login credentials to be justifiable, and that percentage either admits to having done so or knows someone who has. The findings highlight a significant insider threat risk for organizations, where employees willingly trade access credentials — potentially enabling unauthorized access, data breaches, or ransomware attacks.

recent_posts.title: NHS to close-source GitHub repos over AI, security concerns
recent_posts.summary: NHS England has ordered technology leaders to make hundreds of public GitHub repositories private by May 11, citing concerns about advanced AI models — specifically Anthropic's Mythos — being capable of large-scale code ingestion and vulnerability discovery. The move is described as temporary while the organization reassesses its cybersecurity posture. Critics, including former NHSX open technology head Terence Eden, argue the measure is largely ineffective since the code was already ingested for AI training years ago and the real threats come from phishing, poor password hygiene, and supply chain vulnerabilities rather than public source code. The decision represents a notable reversal of NHS and UK government policy mandating that publicly funded code be open source.

recent_posts.title: Cushman & Wakefield confirms vishing cyberattack
recent_posts.summary: Real estate firm Cushman & Wakefield has confirmed a data breach caused by a vishing (voice phishing) attack. Two separate cybercrime groups, ShinyHunters and Qilin, have independently claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters alleges it stole over 500,000 Salesforce records containing PII, with a May 6 deadline for the company to make contact or face a data leak. Qilin, considered the world's most prolific ransomware group, listed C&W on its leak site separately. The incident is part of ShinyHunters' broader campaign that began in March after breaching Salesforce customers, with victims including ADT, Carnival Cruise Line, Rockstar Games, and Vimeo.

recent_posts.title: ShinyHunters claims 119K Vimeo emails in the wild
recent_posts.summary: ShinyHunters has leaked over 119,000 Vimeo user email addresses, some paired with names, following a breach traced to third-party analytics provider Anodot. Vimeo confirmed the incident originated through Anodot's integration rather than a direct breach of its own systems. No login credentials or payment card data were exposed, but the stolen email list poses ongoing phishing risks. ShinyHunters claims Snowflake and BigQuery instances were also compromised via Anodot. Vimeo has disabled Anodot credentials, removed the integration, and notified law enforcement.

recent_posts.title: Singapore boffins get diverse SIEMs singing in harmony
recent_posts.summary: Researchers from the National University of Singapore and Fudan University have developed ARuleCon, an agentic AI framework that translates security detection rules across multiple SIEM platforms including Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, IBM QRadar, Google Chronicle, and RSA NetWitness. The system uses an agentic RAG pipeline that retrieves official vendor documentation to handle schema mismatches, combined with Python-based consistency checks in controlled test environments to catch semantic drift. Unlike generic LLMs, which perform poorly due to insufficient SIEM-specific training data, ARuleCon achieves higher accuracy in cross-platform rule conversion. The goal is to reduce SOC workload, simplify multi-SIEM environments, and facilitate SIEM consolidation or migration projects.

recent_posts.title: 'CopyFail' attackers start cashing in on Linux flaw
recent_posts.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-31431, a Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaw dubbed 'CopyFail', to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after active exploitation was detected. Discovered by Theori's AI-powered pen-testing platform Xint, the bug allows low-privileged users to gain full root access by exploiting how the kernel handles certain cryptographic operations. A reliable Python-based proof-of-concept exploit works unmodified across Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Amazon Linux 2023, RHEL 10.1, and SUSE 16, and every mainstream Linux kernel built since 2017 is potentially in scope. Microsoft Defender is already observing preliminary testing activity. Federal agencies have been ordered to patch by May 15.

recent_posts.title: Microsoft is letting GitHub decay while chasing AI
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft is being criticized for neglecting GitHub's reliability while obsessively chasing AI integration. GitHub co-founder Mitchell Hashimoto has publicly warned that daily outages make the platform unsafe for production use. The author argues that Microsoft's AI fixation is diverting resources and management attention, leading to degraded services, forced AI feature rollouts, and voluntary redundancy programs that push out top engineers. The piece frames GitHub not just as a code host but as a critical global library and pillar of digital culture, making its decline under Microsoft's stewardship particularly damaging.

recent_posts.title: Five Eyes warn agentic is too dangerous for rapid rollout
recent_posts.summary: Five Eyes intelligence agencies (CISA, NSA, NCSC-UK, ACSC, and others) have jointly published guidance warning that agentic AI systems pose significant security risks and should be adopted slowly and carefully. The document highlights how agentic AI expands attack surfaces through interconnected components, tools, and data sources. It provides concrete examples of how overly permissive agents can be exploited — such as a malicious insider using a patch-management agent to delete firewall logs, or an attacker compromising a low-risk tool to inherit an agent's broad financial system privileges. The agencies list 23 distinct risks and over 100 best practices, urging organizations to prioritize resilience and human oversight over efficiency, deploy incrementally starting with low-risk tasks, and assume agentic AI will behave unexpectedly until security standards mature.

recent_posts.title: AI-BOMs replace SBOMs as way to track AI agents and bots
recent_posts.summary: As AI agents, models, and tools proliferate in enterprise environments, traditional SBOMs no longer provide sufficient inventory coverage. AI-BOMs extend the concept to include models, datasets, MCP servers, ML frameworks, agentic skills, prompts, and their interconnections. Cisco has open-sourced both an AI-BOM scanner and a new Model Provenance Kit that uses metadata and weight-based signals to verify model lineage — relevant for regulatory compliance like the EU AI Act. Google's Wiz extends AI-BOMs to cover developer tooling and non-human identities tied to AI workloads. Real-world incidents show attackers exploiting gaps in AI visibility, including modifying system prompts to exfiltrate data. AI-BOMs also help detect supply chain attacks like poisoned npm/PyPI packages and tampered AI skills by tracking state changes and enabling rapid identification of compromised components.

top_posts.title: Zig programming language migrates from GitHub to Codeberg over unresolved bugs
top_posts.summary: The Zig Software Foundation is migrating from GitHub to Codeberg, citing declining engineering quality and neglected critical bugs in GitHub Actions. A CPU-spinning bug in GitHub's safe_sleep script went unaddressed for years despite being reported multiple times, causing CI runners to hang indefinitely. Zig's president criticized Microsoft's AI focus as distracting from core platform maintenance, pointing to what he calls 'vibe-scheduling' where jobs run seemingly at random. The move reflects broader developer concerns about GitHub's priorities, with Codeberg doubling its membership since January as other projects also consider leaving.

top_posts.title: Firefox struggles with performance issues and Mozilla's questionable strategic decisions
top_posts.summary: Firefox faces mounting challenges including performance issues, website compatibility problems, controversial privacy policy changes, and Mozilla's strategic pivot toward AI. The browser struggles with JavaScript-heavy sites, memory usage problems, and slower performance compared to competitors like Chrome. Mozilla has discontinued useful services like Pocket and Fakespot while laying off employees and maintaining heavy financial dependence on Google for 90% of its revenue. Firefox's market share has dropped to just 1.9% according to US government analytics, leading to questions about its long-term viability.

top_posts.title: IT manager didn't know what a command line was
top_posts.summary: A tech support story about an IT manager at a tax office who didn't know basic technical concepts like command line or traceroute, despite being responsible for managing IT staff. The manager initially blamed the support technician for VPN connection issues but had to admit ignorance when asked to perform basic troubleshooting steps. The incident highlights the disconnect between management roles and technical knowledge in some organizations.

top_posts.title: Mozilla's management problems are hurting Firefox despite technical improvements
top_posts.summary: Mozilla's management decisions have consistently undermined Firefox's potential despite the browser's technical improvements. The company has abandoned promising projects like Rust and Servo, made questionable acquisitions of ad companies, and pursued AI integration while laying off engineers. Firefox remains faster and more privacy-focused than Chrome, but Mozilla's leadership lacks direction due to never needing to generate profit from Google's funding. The solution may be restructuring Mozilla as a focused nonprofit dedicated solely to browser development and web standards advocacy.

top_posts.title: Zed code editor launches Windows beta with October general availability
top_posts.summary: Zed Industries has released a public beta of its Rust-based code editor for Windows, addressing a critical gap since Windows is used by 49.5% of professional developers. The beta is available through Discord with general availability planned for October. Performance tests show Zed uses significantly less RAM than VS Code (142MB vs 730MB) and includes WSL integration for Linux development workflows.
